result_text:
Template literals are now ignored when units are compared for duplication, so JavaScript functions that differ only inside a backtick literal are reported as one duplicated unit. The `*AnalyzerTest` and `*UnitsExtractorTest` classes in `codeanalyzer` pass. I didn't run the rest of the module's tests.

- **Fix:** `extraCleanContent` in `codeanalyzer/.../units/CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java` now has one more line, `replaceAll("`.*?`", "``")`. It sits next to the existing `"..."` and `'...'` replacements, so a template literal becomes an empty one, `${...}` interpolations included. Unit duplicates are built from the cleaned body that this method produces.
- **Test:** I added `extractUnitsIgnoresTemplateLiteralContent` to `JavaScriptAnalyzerTest`. It checks that two functions differing only in the literal text get identical cleaned bodies. It also checks that a difference outside the literal (`a = 1` versus `a = 2`) still gives different bodies.
- **Limitation:** like the other literal patterns, this matches within a single line. A template literal that spans several lines is not masked.
- **Other languages:** the change is in the shared C-style extractor, so any language using it also treats backtick text as a literal. Go raw strings are one example.

I didn't commit anything.
